findings.submittalTypeInvariance: CONFIRMED LIVE, not just from source: all 4 samples, across 2 real parcels in 2 different zoning districts and 4 different declared projectType strings, produced byte-identical section/bookId/determination/citation-presence shapes. Declared submittal type has zero live effect on coverage.

sectionReferenceCoverage.denominator: distinct UDC sections named in the real zoning-fact atom's codeSectionRefs, sampled on 2 real parcels
sectionReferenceCoverage.detail: 14-02-003 (districtRequirements) and 14-02-008 (permittedUseTable) -- both present in CODE_BOOKS['BASTROP-UDC']. No missing section numbers exist at this level; the WDLL's literal framing ("the specific missing section numbers") does not describe the real gap.

sectionAdjudicationCoverage.detail: 14-02-003 can reach a real Pass/Fail (adjudicateMinimumSetback). 14-02-008 has a real citation but NO adjudication logic anywhere in the codebase and stays permanently Unchecked -- by design, not by missing content. This is arguably the highest-consequence gap of the three reported here: whether a proposed use is even PERMITTED in the district is never checked, for any submittal type, on any parcel, today.

dimensionAdjudicationCoverage.denominator: real numeric fields present on the setback-rule atom (front, side, rear, sideInteriorFt, sideCornerFt, maxHeightFt; minLotSize excluded as non-setback)
missingDimensions: min lot size (a distinct dimension, not a setback, also unadjudicated)
dimensionAdjudicationCoverage.detail: Only proposedSetbackFrontFt vs setback-rule.front is ever compared. The other five real, ordinance-sourced fields are fetched and stored but never read by any adjudication path. Confirmed present on both sampled parcels/districts with different real values.

unresolvedSourceConflict.sf1_parcel_48021_34737: adjudicated front/side/rear (25/5/25, city GIS layer 23) disagrees with the same city's own Revisions layer 83 (30/10/20/30) -- unresolved in the source data itself, named there ('verify which is in effect with the city'), never actioned by this program.
unresolvedSourceConflict.mu_parcel_48021_34177: adjudicated maxHeightFt (40, layer 23) disagrees with layer 83 (45) -- same unresolved-conflict pattern, different dimension.
unresolvedSourceConflict.implication: Even the one dimension that IS adjudicated (front setback) may be checked against a non-authoritative number for an unknown fraction of Bastrop parcels. Not measured here how many of Bastrop's parcels carry this conflict -- named as a real open question, not a number fabricated to fill this gap.

howThisCouldStillGoWrong: Only 2 of Bastrop's real parcels were sampled (one per zoning district found). The 2-section / 1-adjudicated-dimension shape held on both, and codeSectionRefs is structurally the same across districts (generic pointers, not per-district section numbers), so a third district is unlikely to differ -- but not sampled, named as a limit rather than silently generalized further.

The unresolved-source-conflict finding is reported as PRESENT on both sampled parcels, not as a citywide rate -- no measurement was taken of what fraction of Bastrop's parcel population carries a layer-23-vs-layer-83 conflict.
